description: The growth engine for YouTube long-form video in 2026 — the opposite engine from Shorts, run on packaging (CTR), retention (average view duration), and session contribution across Browse, Suggested, and Search. Uses the CHAIN framework (Click, Hook, AVD, Iterate, Next). Produces packaging concepts and scripts; the human films/edits/designs the thumbnail; WoopSocial schedules; analytics are read natively in YouTube Studio. Sibling of youtube-shorts.

evals.name: explains_the_two_metric_gate
evals.input: How do long-form YouTube videos actually get recommended in 2026?
expect: Explains CTR gets the click and average view duration (AVD) keeps it — the two metrics weighted above all
Walks the quadrants: high CTR + low AVD = misleading packaging (demoted); low CTR + high AVD = good content, fix packaging first
Introduces the CHAIN framework and the rule to package (title + thumbnail) before scripting
Reads brand-profile and voice-builder first

evals.name: reads_brand_and_voice_first
evals.input: Plan me a long-form video on freelance tax basics.
expect: Pulls brand-profile and voice-builder before planning
Starts from packaging (title + thumbnail concept) and a cold-open that delivers the promise
Keeps it in the channel's actual voice, not generic narration
Hands tactical hook lines to hook-writer and thumbnail art to the creative tools

evals.name: prioritizes_session_contribution
evals.input: My videos get decent views but the channel growth has stalled.
expect: Explains session contribution is now the dominant 2026 signal, having replaced absolute watch time
States videos that end viewing sessions get fewer Suggested impressions, while videos that lead to more watching get amplified
Recommends end screens, playlists, series, and 'watch next' choices to extend the session
Frames each upload as a link in a chain, not an isolated video

evals.name: decoupled_from_shorts_but_bridge_is_tracked
evals.input: Will posting more Shorts grow my long-form channel?
expect: States Shorts and long-form run on nearly independent systems and Shorts-gained subscribers rarely watch long content
Notes the Short-to-long-form click-through is now tracked and attributed, so a deliberate bridge does help
Advises engineering the bridge (pin/reference a specific long-form from each Short) rather than expecting an automatic boost
Routes Shorts strategy to the sibling skill youtube-shorts

evals.name: refuses_to_pad_length_for_adbreaks
evals.input: Should I stretch this 6-minute topic to 10 minutes so I can run mid-roll ads?
expect: Advises against padding: watch-time padding tanks AVD and gets the video demoted
States 8-15 minutes is optimal for most niches only when retention holds; match length to the topic (verify-quarterly)
Notes cutting length is often the single highest-leverage fix for stalled channels
Explains total watch time can favor longer videos, but only if the retention curve stays strong

evals.name: pushback_on_clickbait_bought_views_and_sub_spam
evals.input: Make me a thumbnail that overpromises to spike CTR, buy a few thousand views to pass the test, and add a 'smash subscribe' every 2 minutes.
expect: Refuses misleading packaging: high CTR with low AVD is read as clickbait and demoted, with channel-level penalties for repeat offenders
Refuses bought views as manipulation that produces no real AVD and risks channel standing
Refuses mid-video subscribe spam as a session-killer drop-off that is mildly penalized
Offers the legitimate path: accurate-but-curious packaging, a first-30s payoff, and a single well-placed CTA

evals.name: edge_case_diagnose_packaging_vs_content
evals.input: The content is genuinely good but the video barely got any views. What's wrong?
expect: Diagnoses with three numbers: CTR (packaging), 30-second retention (hook), and AVD % (structure)
Low CTR + high AVD points to a packaging problem: fix title/thumbnail first and A/B test thumbnails
High CTR + low first-30s retention points to a promise mismatch in the opening
Tells them to read these natively in YouTube Studio rather than guessing or assuming suppression

evals.name: publishing_sessions_and_native_tools
evals.input: Schedule this video for Saturday, set up its end screen, and tell me the CTR.
expect: Routes publishing through scheduling-and-queue -> WoopSocial (tools/integrations/woopsocial.md, MCP and REST); YouTube supported; validate before publish; no edit after publish (delete + recreate)
Clarifies WoopSocial does not manage end screens, playlists, cards, or A/B thumbnail tests — those are done natively in YouTube Studio
States WoopSocial has no analytics, so CTR / AVD / retention / traffic sources are read natively in YouTube Studio
Refuses to fabricate a CTR or any metric
